saints.name: St. Lydia
saints.title: Disciple of St. Paul
saints.shortBlurb: A seller of purple cloth at Philippi who became the first recorded convert to Christ in Europe…
biography: Lydia was a businesswoman from Thyatira in Asia Minor, a dealer in the costly purple dye, who had settled at Philippi in Macedonia. As recounted in the Acts of the Apostles, she was among the women gathered for prayer by the riverside when St. Paul preached there, and 'the Lord opened her heart' to heed his words.

She and her household were baptized, becoming the first Christians of the European continent, and she pressed the apostles to lodge in her home. When Paul and Silas were released from the Philippian prison, it was again to Lydia's house that they returned, so that her household became the cradle of the church at Philippi.
saints.knownFor: Being the first convert to Christianity in Europe.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 3 August
